thread.title_full: Hargett's pitching, walking lead to Darlington win - NewsBreak

author: Matthew Brown
title: Hargett's pitching, walking lead to Darlington win - NewsBreak
text:
By Matthew Brown ,
5 hours ago Coosa’s Jaurice Warren rounds first base and heads to second for a double in Tuesday’s home game against Region 7A D-I leader Gordon Lee. By Steven Eckhoff A walk-off win in baseball is a walk-off win, even if the walk-off is in the form of a ... walk.
Darlington School’s Thomas Hargett not only ensured that he and his Tiger teammates would get to a second extra-inning with a chance to win, but he drove in that game-winning run Tuesday by drawing the bases-loaded walk in the bottom half of the ninth inning. With that, Darlington defeated visiting Haralson County High 3-2 to get both their overall season record (9-9) and Region 6A D-I mark (5-5) back to the .500 level.
Cooper Norris pitched into the seventh inning Tuesday but could not get an out; a slim 2-1 lead slipped away from the home crowd. Rebel Keaton King hit a double, then the visitors scored the tying run via an error in the Tiger infield. That prompted the pitching change from Tiger coach Matt Larry.
Hargett would complete three shutout innings on the mound without giving up a hit, walking one and striking out one.
Norris and Haralson’s Tyler McCoy engaged in a quality pitcher’s duel with nothing happening on the offensive side for two innings. The only hit was by Darlington’s Braxton Stegall leading off the home half of the second, but McCoy induced a 6-4-3 double play.
The Rebels would strike first in terms of scoring, and just like in the seventh inning a miscue allowed them to break the scoreless deadlock. Preston Dempsey led off the top of the third with his team’s first hit but was retired when Norris got the ensuing bunt for a force out at second. Landon Wright next delivered a hit for Haralson, but then the Tigers were in position for its own inning-ending double play.
They got one out but botched the relay to first base, and Wright hustled around to home plate.
Norris, down 1-0, led off Darlington’s half of the third and tripled thanks to a mis-timed dive in center field. Following a walk, Mac Cannon put down a bunt McCoy fielded but held on to as all Tigers advanced one base. That included the tying run for 1-1.
Still with nobody out and the bases loaded, Haralson County turned its second double play of the game but gave up the lead run in the process. The inning ended with two Tigers still in scoring position.
The game settled back down to a pitchers’ duel. Darlington had only one hit over its next three turns, that being a lead-off single by Henry Ledbetter in the fourth.
It was Haralson County that threatened, and threatened, and threatened some more before their efforts finally paid off in the seventh. Over the fifth and sixth innings, seven out of eight batters reached base, none of which scored. It all started with a one-out walk in the top of the fifth, but Norris picked that Rebel off first base.
Three more hits followed, but Wilson Lucas threw out King at home plate from right field for out No. 3.
Three out of the first four Rebel batters of the sixth singled to load the bases with one out, but then Norris recorded his seventh strikeout and added another assist to end the inning still up 2-1.
Darlington and Haralson County have two more Region 6A D1 baseball games to play, which will be during a doubleheader in Tallapoosa on Friday.
Other results
In a battle of two teams eyeing the first-place position in 6A D-I, Pepperell High went to Franklin on Tuesday and destroyed the Heard County Braves 15-1 on 16 hits, two of which were home runs. The Dragons improved to 12-8 and 7-3, and it was Heard’s second region loss against five wins.
The home runs for Pepperell were a grand slam by Tucker Glenn and one by Madoc Garcia, who had three RBIs and four runs scored. Aaron Wood drove in two runs, Cade McElwee was 3-for-3 with an RBI and Chance Hopper had two hits with an RBI.
Pepperell and Heard County play two games in the Lindale community Friday beginning at 5 p.m.
In Region 7A D-I, things went well for Armuchee High starting three straight games against Gordon Central. The Indians went to Calhoun and won 15-3 in five innings. It was 9-0 after the first and 11-0 after three.
Armuchee (6-12, 4-6) hosts Gordon Central on Thursday at 5 p.m. and then plays again in Calhoun on Friday.
Coosa High, however, was a 16-0 five-inning victim to 7A D-I leader Gordon Lee (10-0) at home Tuesday. It was the Eagles’ sixth loss in a row dropping them to 4-14. Jaurice Warren of Coosa had two hits, one a double.
Gordon Lee hosts Coosa in Chickamauga on Friday for a doubleheader.
